title: Can a Fresh Start Really Change You?
html:
Good morning,

When someone seems confident and successful, it’s easy to believe they’ve got themselves sorted.

I did.

My business partner was the best sales trainer I’d ever seen. He could walk into a room of strangers and have them laughing and buying within twenty minutes.

I watched him and thought, if we could build a business around that ability, we’d do well.

So we started one together - The New Zealand Sales Institute. And it was an instant success!

Then I began finding things in the accounts that didn’t add up. Money was coming in, but it was going back out on rent, vehicles and restaurants.

He had an explanation for everything and a vision that was compelling. So, I stayed another six months.

That’s the part I still find hard to admit. I could see the signs, but I kept finding reasons to believe him.

Later, I learned he’d left large debts behind in Australia and America. Coming to New Zealand had given him a chance to stay below the radar.

Then someone from Australia spotted what he was doing.

For years, I looked at this story through what he’d done to me. Recently, I’ve tried looking at it through his eyes.

What did he want? What was he afraid of?

I can’t know exactly. But I imagine the chance to build something again was hard to resist. A new country. A business partner who believed in him. People who didn’t know his history.

Perhaps he wanted a fresh start while fearing the past would catch up with him.

Before, I saw a confident, successful man. Now, I wonder how much of that confidence was covering fear.

That doesn’t excuse what he did. But it gives me another layer to understand him.

It also reminds me of a saying:

“Wherever you go, there you are.”

He’d changed countries. But the behaviour that had caused problems came with him.

We can do smaller versions of that ourselves. Change jobs. Move house. Start another business. Expect the new circumstances to fix an old pattern.

Sometimes a fresh start helps. But we still have to do the work of changing.

Confidence doesn’t tell you whether someone has made peace with themselves. Sometimes the boldest move is an attempt to outrun something they’re afraid to face.

And wherever they go, there they are.

To your success!

Glenn
